Numbered chapter 2:
[1] He crossed the rise at a stumble and from the crest saw it: a dark mound in the white, too regular to be rock.
[2] He went down.
[3] Snow had drifted against one flank; the matted coat held the animal’s shape like a cast.
[4] A woolly mammoth.
[5] Its trunk lay curled against the snow, one tusk sheared near the root.
[6] The body was whole—no cuts, no spear marks, no trampled ring where hunters had stood.
[7] Nothing had fed on it.
[8] It had lain down, or been caught, and the cold had kept it.
[9] He stood a long time.
[10] The wind worked at his coat.
[11] He had aimed for the late Pleistocene—the caves, the fires, the people he had spent his life studying.
[12] This was older.
[13] Tens of thousands of years older.
[14] The jump had missed, or he had, and the error was not one he could walk back from.
[15] He had given everything to arrive, and here it was: a dead thing in the snow and no one to meet him.
[16] He crouched.
[17] His hands were clumsy, but he worked a shard of rib free and tore a strip of hide from the flank, stiff as board.
[18] He wrapped the hide around his wrist and put the bone in his coat.
[19] Then he looked at the ravine beyond the rise and started walking.
